newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IDT taps funds in Singapore for growth.
newsitem.headline: IDT taps funds in Singapore for growth.

text.p: IDT Holdings (Singapore) Ltd, a unit of Hong Kong's IDT International, offered shares in Singapore on Wednesday to raise funds to attack the growing market in LCD (liquid crystal display) consumer electronics.
"Singapore is a country that values manufacturing and marketing companies somewhat higher than Hong Kong does as a bourse," IDT group managing director Barry Buttifant told Reuters in an interview.

IDT's Singapore unit is offering 22.08 million shares at US$0.73 each, with a placement tranche of 17.664 million shares, in its initial public offer (IPO). Half of the offer is made up of vendor shares which are existing stocks, and the rest are new shares.
Proceeds of US$7.1 million from new shares would be used to expand production facilities in China, build a bigger marketing and distribution network and for working capital.

The company, which designs, manufactures and markets LCD consumer electronic products, is the biggest revenue contributor to IDT International -- HK$417 million (US$54 million), or 40 percent of turnover for the financial year that ended March 1996.
"It is the most profitable business of IDT International," said Buttifant.

He said IDT Singapore aimed to maintain an annual turnover growth rate of slightly more than 10 percent, based on its annual compound turnover growth rate of 11 percent achieved in the 1992-1996 financial years.
For the year ending March 1997, the company projected a 19 percent net profit growth to HK$54 million. Turnover is forecast to rise 12 percent to HK$469 million.

IDT was mainly an original design manufacturer, meaning it did everything from coming up with the idea to final manufacture. This gave it better profits than original equipment manufacturers with margins often as low as five percent, Buttifant said.
He said demand for LCD electronic products was fuelled by technological advancement in LCD products and wider range of applications.
Besides its mainstay of measuring, timing and healthcare devices, IDT was venturing into new LCD applications such as smart card readers, he said.
Buttifant said IDT expected significant contracts for smart card readers and vendor terminals in Japan and Europe which would contribute to profits in the 1997-1998 financial year.
IDT would introduce 55 new products in the 1997 financial year, after launching 86 new items over the past two years, officials said at the IPO briefing.
All of IDT's production is at its plant in Xixian in China, which rolls out 500,000 units per month on an extended one-shift basis.
While 54 percent of revenue came from Europe, Buttifant said Europe was not a mature market.
"You can't talk about maturity in a market in terms of like TV sets or audios ... the marketplace and applications of the products change a great deal."
He saw "significant growth" in North America in terms of market penetration where IDT chalked up 29 percent of sales.

IDT was looking to develop the gift market in Asia, he said. Eventually, IDT would like one-third of its business to come from each of the three regions of Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, said Buttifant.
